transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I’m here because I can’t keep being brushed off about my dad’s lab results. For about a year now I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing things, or holding back parts of his results. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family, all of them—but I know what I saw, and the chart doesn’t match. 

I work around blood draws, so I’m not just making things up, and I know people think I’m being difficult, but it’s been wearing me down. I just need someone to actually listen.
Do you think someone is intentionally changing your dad's lab results?

Yes. I mean… I don’t know who exactly, but I do think someone in that clinic system is changing something, or leaving parts out. Because I saw what I saw, and then later the chart didn’t match, and everyone keeps acting like I’m confused.

And I work around blood draws, so it’s not like I don’t understand how results are supposed to show up. I know sometimes clerical things happen, people put stickers in the wrong place—actually at work once we had this whole thing with mislabeled tubes and everyone acted like it was no big deal—but this feels different. This has been going on for about a year, and no matter how many doctors or my family say, “The numbers are fine,” it doesn’t line up. It’s just… wearing me down.
Do you think this is happening to you and your dad specifically, or could it be a broader conspiracy?

I think it’s us. I mean, my dad’s results are the ones I’ve been watching, and that’s where the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I’m not saying I know it’s some huge thing with everybody, but… clinic systems are messy, you know? I work around blood draws, and people act like paperwork and labels and charts are just magically correct every time.

But for the past year, I’ve been trying to prove that something is being changed or held back with his labs specifically. And every time I bring it up, doctors and my family say the numbers are fine, like that should settle it. It doesn’t, because I know what I saw. It’s been wearing me down.
Have you ever considered the possibility that you might be mistaken about the lab results?

I mean… I’ve tried to ask myself that, because everyone keeps saying it like I’m just stressed or reading it wrong. But then I come back to the same thing: I know what I saw, and the chart later didn’t match it.

And it’s not like I’m some random person who’s never been around labs. I’m a phlebotomist, I know how results and samples are supposed to work—well, mostly, I mean there’s always paperwork stuff, and people rushing, and computers being slow, and at my job there are days where the labels pile up and you just think, how does anything stay straight? But with my dad’s labs, this has been going on for a year. I keep trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding parts back, and doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine.

So… mistaken? I guess I’ve considered it because people keep pushing that on me. But I don’t believe that’s what this is. It’s wearing me down.
Would you change your mind about someone altering your dad's lab results if you were shown proof that the results are accurate?

If it was real proof, I mean… I’d want to see it myself, not just have someone tell me, “It’s fine.” That’s what keeps happening, and then I’m supposed to just drop it.

Because I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And everyone keeps saying the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It just doesn’t.

So would I change my mind? I don’t know. Maybe if I could really see everything from start to finish, like the actual process, not just a printout after the fact. At work, I’ve seen how things can get missed when people are rushing, and then everyone acts like the computer is the truth. That’s the part that makes me feel like I can’t just accept it. It’s been wearing me down.
Would you say that no amount of evidence could ever change your mind about someone altering your dad's lab results?

I wouldn’t say no amount, exactly… but it would have to be more than people just telling me I’m wrong. Because that’s what keeps happening, and then they act like I’m being difficult.

I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And I know everyone says the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but I saw something different, and then the chart didn’t match. That’s not nothing.

At work, even with little things, labels, tubes, computers… people think it’s all clean and perfect, but it isn’t always. So when they just show me the chart after the fact, I can’t just accept that as proof. It’s been wearing me down, honestly. So… I guess I’m not saying impossible, but I don’t know what would make me fully believe them unless I could really see how it all happened.
Do you think you would ever be able to accept that your dad's lab results are accurate, even if multiple people and evidence confirm it?

I don’t know… I mean, if multiple people said it, that’s already kind of what’s been happening, right? Doctors say it, my family says it, and I’m supposed to just nod and be relieved, but I can’t get past what I saw.

For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding parts of my dad’s labs back. And I know that sounds exhausting—because it is, it’s completely wearing me down—but the chart doesn’t match what I remember seeing. At work, even just with regular draws, things get messy, labels, computers, people rushing… and then everyone acts like once it’s in the system it’s untouchable.

So could I ever accept it? Maybe I want to say yes, because I don’t want to keep living like this. But if the “evidence” is just more people showing me the same chart and telling me the numbers are fine, then no, I don’t think I could just accept that.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you could be wrong about your dad's lab results being altered?

I mean… a possibility? I guess technically people can be wrong. I’m not trying to say I’m perfect or that I remember every single number like a machine. But then I go back to what I saw, and the chart just doesn’t line up with it.

That’s the part everyone skips over. They say, “The doctors reviewed it,” or my family says, “You need to let this go,” but for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that clinic system changed something or held part of my dad’s labs back. And I know how clinics are, I work around blood draws and paperwork and computers, and people act like the system can’t be touched once it’s entered, but that’s not real life.

So… could I be wrong in some tiny way? Maybe. But I don’t feel wrong. I feel like I’m the only one not pretending the chart matches what I saw, and it’s wearing me down.
Do you think about your dad's lab results being altered every day?

Every day? Yeah… I mean, maybe not every single minute, but it’s there every day. I’ll be doing something normal, like at work with tubes or labels, and then I start thinking about how easy it is for something to not match later.

And then with my dad’s labs, that’s the thing—I’ve spent basically the past year trying to prove someone in that clinic system changed something or held part of it back. People keep saying the numbers are fine, the doctors checked it, my family says I’m wearing myself out, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

So yes, I think about it every day. It’s exhausting.
Would your belief about your dad's lab results being altered change if you were given a detailed explanation of how the lab results are handled and verified?

I mean, a detailed explanation might help me understand the process, sure. I know there are checks and steps and people sign off on things—I’m a phlebotomist, I’ve seen how much of it is supposed to be tracked. But that’s also why it bothers me, because I know systems still have people in them, and people can change things or leave things out.

And I keep coming back to the same thing, even if everyone wants me to move on: I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in that clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors, family, everybody keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

So would an explanation change it? I don’t know. Maybe it would calm me for a little while, but if it doesn’t explain that mismatch, then no… I don’t think it would really change what I believe. It’s wearing me down, honestly.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results would ever change, no matter what evidence or explanations you receive?

I don’t know how to answer “ever,” because that feels like you’re asking me to promise I’d ignore proof, and I’m not trying to be unreasonable. I work with lab stuff, you know, tubes and labels and people initialing things, and sometimes people act like computers make everything clean, but half the time it’s still a person clicking the button.

But with my dad’s chart… I keep coming back to it. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that clinic system changed something or held parts of his labs back. And no matter how many doctors tell me the numbers are fine, or my family tells me I’m exhausting myself, I know what I saw. The chart doesn’t match that.

So… if someone could actually explain that, maybe. But if it’s just more “trust us, it’s fine,” then no, I don’t think it would change. It’s worn me down too much to just drop it.
Do you think there will ever be a point where you stop thinking about your dad's lab results being altered?

I want there to be a point. I really do, because I’m tired. Like, I’ll be drawing blood at work and I’ll see how a label prints or how someone sets something down for just a second, and my brain goes right back to it—even if I was thinking about groceries or my car needing an oil change or whatever.

But I don’t know how I stop when nobody has actually explained the part that doesn’t match. I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in that clinic system changed something or held back parts of my dad’s lab results. And everyone—doctors, my family—keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but I know what I saw in the chart. It doesn’t match.

So… maybe if that got answered for real, maybe I could stop. But right now, no. It’s still there, and it’s wearing me down.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results being altered is based on facts or is it just a feeling you have?

It’s facts to me. I know people keep trying to make it sound like it’s just anxiety or me getting stuck on something, but I’m not just making it up out of nowhere.

I work around lab processes, so I know how things are supposed to look, and I know charts don’t just magically feel “off.” There was something that didn’t match what I saw. And then everyone—doctors, my family—keeps saying the numbers are fine, like repeating that is supposed to erase it.

I mean, I get that I probably sound… intense about it. My sister says I go in circles, and maybe I do. I’ll be at work and see a requisition or a label and then I’m thinking about my dad’s chart again instead of what I’m supposed to be doing. But for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in that clinic system changed or held back part of his lab results. That’s not just a feeling. The chart doesn’t match what I saw, and I can’t just ignore that. It’s wearing me down.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results would change if you were shown undeniable proof that they are accurate?

If it was really undeniable, I’d like to say yes. I mean, I’m not trying to be the kind of person who just refuses reality. I work with blood draws and labels and all that, so I know there are procedures, but I also know how easy it is for one little thing to get clicked wrong or filed wrong, and then everyone just keeps moving like nothing happened.

So when you say “undeniable proof,” I start thinking, proof from who? The same clinic system? Because that’s where the problem is. I’ve spent the past year trying to prove someone changed something or held back parts of my dad’s lab results, and everyone keeps telling me, “The numbers are fine,” my family included, but they don’t understand what I saw in the chart. It didn’t match.

Maybe if someone could sit down and actually explain every part of it in a way that made sense, maybe. But if it’s just another printout or another doctor saying it’s accurate, I don’t know. I don’t think I could just let it go. It’s worn me down too much.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results being altered is something that you might be mistaken about, even if you're completely convinced it's true right now?

I mean… I guess anyone can be mistaken, technically. Like, I’ve mislabeled a tube before and caught it right away, so I know people make mistakes both ways. But with this, it doesn’t feel like just me being stubborn.

I’ve been trying for the past year to prove that someone in that clinic system changed something or held back parts of my dad’s lab results. And every time I bring it up, doctors or my family just say the numbers are fine, but that doesn’t answer why the chart didn’t match what I saw. That’s the part I keep coming back to.

So could I be mistaken? I don’t know. Maybe in some broad sense, yes. But right now I’m completely convinced something isn’t right, and it’s… it’s wearing me down.
Do you think there's anything that could happen, or any information you could receive, that would make you completely change your mind about your dad's lab results being altered?

I don’t know what would make me completely change my mind. Maybe if someone outside that whole clinic system could go through it with me, not just hand me another page and say, “See, it’s fine.” But even then, I’d have questions, because the chart did not match what I saw.

And I know I keep saying that, but it’s because that’s the part nobody answers. I’m a phlebotomist, I see how these things move through the system, labels, requisitions, results posting… and then people act like systems can’t hide things or change things just because they’re computerized. That’s not how it works.

Sorry, I’m getting off track. I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system changed or held back part of my dad’s lab results. My family says I’m exhausting myself, doctors say the numbers are fine, but I know what I saw in the chart, and it doesn’t match. So… completely change my mind? I can’t honestly say yes. It’s been wearing me down too much.
Do you think you could ever stop thinking about your dad's lab results being altered, even if you received an explanation for the discrepancy?

I don’t know. I’d want to say yes, because I’m tired of thinking about it. I really am. But even if someone gave me an explanation, I think I’d still be going back over it in my head, like, “Okay, but why did it look different then?” Because the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

And I know people think I’m just stuck on this, but I work around lab stuff, so it’s not like I’m making it up out of nowhere. Labels get scanned, results get posted, people assume the computer is right, and then if you question it you’re the difficult one. I’ve seen little mistakes turn into big confusion before—not with him, I mean just in general at work—and that’s what people don’t understand.

So could I stop thinking about it? Maybe for a little while. But I’ve been trying for the past year to prove that someone in that clinic system changed something or held back part of my dad’s results, and everyone keeps saying the numbers are fine. My family, doctors, everybody. It’s worn me down, but I can’t just turn it off because someone gives me an explanation that still doesn’t fit.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results being altered is something that could be proven or disproven with evidence?

I mean… evidence should prove it, right? That’s what I keep saying. Labs are supposed to be evidence — the chart, the numbers, the timestamps, who entered what. But then when I ask about it, everyone just says, “Your dad’s numbers are fine,” and that’s not the same thing as explaining why the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

Sorry, I know I’m going in circles. It’s just… I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that clinic system changed something or held back parts of my dad’s lab results. And no matter how many doctors or my family tell me it’s fine, I can’t get past that mismatch.

So could it be proven or disproven? Maybe technically, yes, if someone actually showed me the full record and explained every part of it. But the way it’s been handled, it feels like the evidence is exactly what’s being controlled. And that’s what’s wearing me down.
Do you think you might be overestimating the significance of the discrepancy in your dad's lab results due to your own stress or anxiety?

Maybe stress makes it worse, yeah. I’m not saying I’m calm about it. I’m exhausted, and my family keeps telling me I’m making too much of it, and then I start second-guessing how I’m coming across.

But I don’t think stress created the discrepancy. That’s the part I keep trying to explain. I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or held back parts of my dad’s lab results. And every time people say, “The numbers are fine,” it feels like they’re skipping over the actual problem, which is that the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

And I know, I know, I get stuck on details. At work, if a label is off or something posts weird, you don’t just say, “Well, the patient looks fine,” you track it down. That’s what bothers me. So maybe anxiety makes me keep checking it, but I don’t think I’m overestimating it. It’s wearing me down because nobody will really answer it.
Do you think your belief about your dad's lab results is something that you are certain about, and nothing can change your mind?

I don’t want to say “nothing can change my mind,” because that makes me sound unreasonable, and I’m not trying to be. If someone could actually show me what happened—like the full record, the timing, why it looked one way and then another—then maybe that would help.

But… honestly, I feel certain about what I saw. I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And everyone keeps saying, “The numbers are fine,” my family, doctors, everybody, but that’s not the same as explaining why the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

It’s like at work, if a tube label doesn’t match or something posts oddly, you don’t just shrug and say it’s fine. You check the chain of it. And I know that’s not exactly what you asked, sorry. But yes, I guess I do feel pretty certain. It’s wearing me down, because I keep trying to let it go and then I come back to the same thing: the chart doesn’t match.
